label: G1-blind-cut-and-harden
prompt: You are an INDEPENDENT senior systems architect + security reviewer giving a BLIND take. Do NOT assume a predetermined answer. GROUND (facts only): 'YURI-OS' is one solo technical founder's large personal AI operating system + a personal agent 'Yuri' (voice+text, GLM-5.2 brain, full bash, document parsing, screen reading, multi-lane sub-agent dispatch). It has grown big: ~594 scripts in _SYSTEM/Scripts, 44 hooks (only ~3 actually block; the rest advisory), 107 skills, ~320 memory files, a ~404-line identity layer loaded every session, and a REGEX confirm-gate (not sandboxed). The owner wants it SIMPLER but MORE POWERFUL, with deep structural cleanup and real security. TASK: produce YOUR OWN opinionated answer to: 'If you had to cut YURI to its powerful core and harden the agent, what would you do?' Cover: (1) the 5 highest-leverage STRUCTURAL cuts/consolidations (what overlapping subsystems to collapse), (2) the 5 highest-leverage SECURITY hardening moves for an agent with these capabilities, (3) the ONE compounding change that makes everything after it easier, (4) an explicit 'do NOT cut / do NOT touch' list (the load-bearing core + anything where cutting risks breakage). Be concrete and divergent — your value is a genuinely independent take whose DIFFERENCE from other lanes is the signal. Read code to ground yourself where useful, but do not just inventory — RULE.

label: G2-blind-compounding-simplification
prompt: You are an independent reviewer giving a BLIND take. GROUND: a solo founder's large personal AI-OS (~594 scripts, 44 hooks, 107 skills, ~320 memory files, multiple overlapping dispatch + gate + memory subsystems) with a personal agent front-end. His north star: 'I think and speak and it gets done', across parallel sessions + overnight runs, with LESS friction and MORE power. TASK: name the SINGLE highest-leverage COMPOUNDING simplification (and at most 2 runners-up) — the change that makes every future task simpler AND makes the system more powerful, and that reduces the owner's cognitive load the most. For each: what it is, why it compounds (how it makes the next thing easier), the smallest version that ships, and what it unblocks. Be ruthless about leverage — reject changes that are merely 'nice'. Concrete and opinionated; do not hedge to a generic answer.
